items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: Connie Landers, that was the banjo player, he quit. ... And so he took me and Snake, the trumpet player, Roy White, and the banjo player, Landers. ... Connie Landers on banjo.

ctx.x: So now you're into December what, '28?

'27. And we all left the Virginia Ravens, seven of us left at once, Roy, the trumpet player left, we had a tenor saxophone player named Birdson, and I left. And Edgar Pillows had come in, I had gotten him a job playing bass in the band. He left with us. In fact, we just quit, all of us. Connie Landers, that was the banjo player, he quit. And so when they left us in Shell Lake, Wisconsin, they only had about three men left. That was the drummer and Joe Thomas and somebody else, because Bill Crump had gone before…
Anyway, we decided to go to Minneapolis, the seven of us. So we bought our tickets, we got on the train and we were headed out to Minneapolis. And we run into a gangster
